chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a slap whose mark turns black on the face that its compensation is six dinars. If it does not turn black but turns green, then its compensation is three dinars. If it turns red and does not turn green, then its compensation is one and a half dinars.
Then he said: As for wounds of the body, retaliation applies in them, unless the injured person accepts the indemnity for the wound, in which case it is given to him.

key_terms.أَرْشَهَا: its assessed financial compensation for injury
key_terms.الْقِصَاصَ: legal retaliation in kind for bodily injury
key_terms.جِرَاحَاتِ: wounds or injuries to the body
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold dinars used as the compensation amount

ai.seo_question: What compensation did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام assign for a slap that leaves marks on the face?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning financial compensation for visible facial injury caused by a slap, with different amounts based on the severity of discoloration. It also states that bodily wounds are subject to qisas, unless the injured party agrees to accept monetary compensation instead.
